author: OpenAxolotl maintainer via the project's hero generator
tool: Blender 4.0.2 headless, tools/blender/make_axolotl.py (deterministic), then rigged by tools/rig_model.py. The mesh is built from skin modifiers over edge skeletons plus subdivision, giving one continuous surface per role (skin, eye, gleam, gill, detail) with named axolotl_<role> materials and vertex-colour albedo. Rigging adds a 12-bone skeleton (root, spine, head, two gills, four legs, three tail segments) with weights from inverse-square distance to the two nearest bones, the eye and its highlight bound whole to the head, and six animation clips (idle, waddle, swim, hop, fall, hurt). 25,256 triangles, inside the character budget of 60,000.
prompt: A cartoon-proportioned axolotl for a family platformer: an oversized broad flat head, a heavy tapering body flowing into a bladed tail fin, six big feathery external gill fronds swept out and back at jaw height, four short splayed legs, dark eyes with baked highlights, and a small mouth and nostrils. Counter-shaded pale pink, belly lighter than the back. Organic form with cartoon proportion — no hard-edged primitives. SUPERSEDES the original upload, a glb from an uncommitted AI-written trimesh script: 85 welded primitives, 13,152 triangles, and no generator in the repo, so no proportion, palette or topology decision could be revisited without hand-editing a binary.
